1. PHYSICIANS earn ~$606B total across facility fees AND professional fees — the highest-paid worker category.
But there are only ~1.1M of them. Per-physician: ~$550K average gross comp (before taxes, loans, malpractice).
2. NURSES & AIDES are the largest workforce (~7M+) and receive ~$700B+ combined — they DO the majority of patient care.
Average RN comp ~$95K; average CNA comp ~$35K. Aides are among the lowest-paid workers in the economy.
3. ADMIN STAFF receive ~$400B+ — billing, coding, prior auth, credentialing, compliance. A uniquely American cost.
The US spends ~15-30% of healthcare $ on administration vs. 2-5% in peer countries (Commonwealth Fund).
4. ~45% of all NHE ($4,541B) goes to healthcare workers. The other ~55% goes to drugs, devices, buildings, IT, capital, and taxes.
This means ~$2.5T/year flows to non-labor costs. Understanding that split is key to "why does a broken arm cost so much?"
